items.bold: TRUMP EDITED US-IRAN AGREEMENT — new demands on uranium + Hormuz "did not go down well in Tehran." MOU: "still, at best, a work in progress." Iran vehemently denied deal.
items.text: CBS News (17 hours ago) confirmed: Trump recently edited the possible US-Iran agreement, including on enriched uranium and the Strait of Hormuz. On Friday, Trump made a series of demands — on the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's nuclear program and the unfreezing of Iranian assets held overseas — that did not go down well in Tehran. So it appears the memorandum of understanding is still, at best, a work in progress. Iran vehemently denied the tentative deal on the Thursday ceasefire extension. The Trump editing signal is the most important new development since Day 90. It confirms: (1) The MOU framework is real but Trump is actively modifying its terms rather than signing as-is. (2) The new demands on enriched uranium likely reflect Netanyahu's influence — the Camp David Cabinet meeting may have produced harder nuclear conditions. (3) Iran's vehement denial suggests the edited terms pushed Iran back from the signing-ready position it had reached. The deal that was "largely negotiated" (Trump, Day 86) is now being re-negotiated by Trump himself.

items.bold: US DEFENSE SECRETARY: Military "ready to resume combat in Gulf if needed." Hezbollah-Israel clashes intensifying. Second front complicating dynamics.
items.text: CNN (1 day ago) confirmed: the US Defense Secretary warned the military is ready to resume combat operations in the Gulf if needed. This statement, alongside Trump's editing of the MOU terms, represents the US dual-track strategy: negotiate AND maintain military pressure simultaneously. The Defense Secretary's warning is directed at Iran: accept Trump's edited terms or face resumed combat. CBS News (17 hours ago) also confirmed: despite the US-mediated ceasefire agreed by Israel and Lebanon in April, clashes between Hezbollah and Israeli forces have intensified, with Israeli troops advancing further into southern Lebanon. The Hezbollah-Israel second front creates additional complications for US-Iran deal dynamics: Iran cannot sign a peace deal with the US while Iran-backed Hezbollah is actively fighting Israel without appearing to abandon its proxy network. This second front is a structural obstacle to a comprehensive settlement.

military.t: TRUMP EDITED MOU — New Demands on Uranium + Hormuz + Asset Unfreezing "Did Not Go Down Well in Tehran." MOU "Work in Progress."
military.d: CBS News (17 hours ago) confirmed: Trump recently edited the possible US-Iran agreement, including on enriched uranium and the Strait of Hormuz. On Friday, Trump made a series of demands — on the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's nuclear program and the unfreezing of Iranian assets held overseas — that did not go down well in Tehran. The MOU is "still, at best, a work in progress." Iran vehemently denied the tentative Thursday ceasefire extension deal. Three categories of new Trump demands: (1) Enriched uranium — likely "unearth and destroy" verification tightened; (2) Strait of Hormuz — likely closing the "Iran+Oman manage" loophole; (3) Iranian asset unfreezing — possibly offered as economic carrot to offset harder nuclear/Hormuz terms. assessment.body:
Tuesday 11:00 AM IST. Day 93. Three signals all pointing the same way.

BRENT $95 AT 11AM
Rebounded from $91.89 Friday close — a $3/barrel rise Tuesday morning.
Economic Times: "conflicting Iran war signals."
The rebound reflects: Trump's edited demands (harder on nuclear/Hormuz), Iran rejecting new terms, peace talks faltering per Asian market reaction.
At $95: OMC losses Rs 12-14/L petrol (worse than near-breakeven at $91), diesel Rs 28-30/L.

NIFTY TECHNICAL — BEARISH SETUP
Zerodha Pulse (5 hours ago): Nifty below key moving averages.
Bollinger Bands trending lower and widening.
Downside momentum intact.
Support: 23,400-23,600. If broken: 23,000-23,200.
The technical picture confirms what the macro picture signals:
deal delay = Brent $93-97 range = OMC pressure = market uncertainty.

ASIAN MARKETS — TALKS FALTERED SIGNAL
Asian markets dipped from record highs as peace talks with Iran faltered.
This is the key phrase — "talks faltered" is the market verdict on
Trump's edited demands + Iran's vehement denial.
US stock futures: slight decline (vs records on Friday).
Gold and silver fell in India — but this is a counterintuitive signal:
gold falling = inflation expectations slightly easing despite Brent $95.

THE MOU STATUS AT 11AM
Work in progress. Trump editing. Iran denying. Both still at table.
US Defense Secretary: combat-ready in Gulf — the "or else" preserved.
The deal will come. The technical picture says India waits.

VERDICT: Day 93 at 11 AM presents three aligned bearish signals:
Brent $95 (up from $91.89), Nifty below moving averages (Bollinger widening),
Asian markets dipping as talks falter.
The edited MOU is the source of all three signals.
When Trump and Iran bridge the edited terms: all three reverse simultaneously.
Until then: India range-bound 23,400-23,800,
Brent $92-97, MOU "work in progress."

featured.title: The Strait of Hormuz and the New Logic of Chokepoint Control
featured.desc: Chokepoint control is no longer binary (open/closed) but a layered spatial contest spanning seabed topology, island sovereignty, electronic warfare, and visibility asymmetry. The cartography of maritime control in the 2026 crisis.

featured.title: Geopolitics of LPG Supply in India
featured.desc: How India's LPG import dependency on the Gulf creates acute vulnerability during the West Asia War. Explores Hormuz exposure, alternative supply routes, and policy imperatives for energy security in a blockade scenario.

featured.title: Geopolitics of Fertiliser Supply in India
featured.desc: India imports 30%+ of its fertilisers via the Strait of Hormuz. This paper maps the supply chain risks to kharif and rabi crops, the strategic case for diversification, and what a prolonged blockade means for food security.
